free_tier.stated: A 30 GB, 7-day try-out: 'The try out plan gives you: 500 mbit speed, 4118 days retention, 30 gigabytes free, No auto billing, Absolutely free'. The vendor's payment FAQ repeats it: 'Can I try your service before I pay? Hell yes! You can always try the first 7 days for free.'

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; no per-object cap is published; the unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, approximately 750 KB by convention, so 1 TiB of monthly transfer corresponds to roughly 1.4 million article fetches
per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: 4118 days retention on the home page and on the try-out page

egress.terms: Unlimited speed on Senior; 40 Mbit on Junior and 80 Mbit on Medior

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563. No HTTP or object API exists for the download path, which is driven through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav.
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: A 30 GB Abavia allowance tests whether an Abavia spool completes the requested content before any money is spent; after that the Junior tier keeps it for EUR 2.46/mo.

limits.value: 25 connections on Junior and Medior, 50 on Senior
40 Mbit Junior, 80 Mbit Medior, unlimited Senior
30 GB on the free try-out, then unlimited on paid plans

limits_note: Junior EUR 2.46/mo (40 Mbit, 25 connections), Medior EUR 3.69/mo (80 Mbit, 25 connections), Senior EUR 5.75/mo (unlimited speed, 50 connections). No automatic renewal: 'Your subscription expires when your subscription days have passed.'
binding_note: The free path is a 30 GB one-off, so at 1 TiB/month the allowance is what fails, and it fails after 30 GB. On Senior the vendor publishes no volume ceiling.

identity_cost.detail: Name, email address, password and country; the form also offers social sign-in. The trial states four gates: no disposable e-mail address, no VPN or proxy server to register, no multiple accounts and no spam domains.

reliability_note: The try-out page also carries the line 'Payment will show up on your statement as NectoFarm B.V.', which is odd for a product listed at 'Total cost: FREE' and suggests a payment method may still be captured. That was not tested at checkout, so it is flagged rather than resolved. Abavia reseller operated by NectoFarm BV. The 30 GB try-out is the largest card-free allowance found on any provider among debrid providers, and the VPN ban is the price of it.
confidence_note: The trial terms, the four registration rules, the prices and the retention figure are all from vendor pages read today. Whether a card is captured at checkout is the one gap, because checkout itself was not tested.
